short: Investigation of Mg-Zn-Y-Nd alloy for potential application
title: Investigation of Mg-Zn-Y-Nd alloy for potential application of biodegradable esophageal stent material

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Esophageal stents of 317L stainless steel stay in the body, are far harder than the tissue and invite restenosis and inflammation. A Mg-Zn-Y-Nd alloy that degrades in the body and alkalinises its surroundings should both disappear on its own and hold back the cells that cause restenosis.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/forming), n7 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: 317L stainless steel esophageal stents stay in place permanently and are associated with restenosis and inflammatory response; Magnesium corrodes in chloride media by releasing Mg2+ and OH-, which raises the local pH; Eca109, L929 and Het-1A cells drive restenosis in an esophageal stent and macrophages drive the inflammatory response; the tumour microenvironment is acidic

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Both discs are smooth at the tens-of-nanometre level, the alloy at 57 nm average roughness with parallel polishing grooves against 32 nm for the steel. Immersion turns the alloy surface into an open, cracked porous corrosion layer by day 15-30, while the steel surface is unchanged

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: The alloy is about a quarter as hard as the steel, 54.3 against 198.7 HV. The alloy surface is markedly less wettable, 59.9 deg water contact angle against 28.4 deg for the steel.
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (PRP/value), n10 (PRP/value), n11 (PRP/value), n13 (PRP/value), n14 (PRP/value), n15 (PRP/value), n16 (MEC/pathway)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: As a stent material the alloy does the job in vitro: it degrades steadily in physiological fluid, is far less hard than the steel, and holds back restenosis-related and inflammatory cells

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd combines degradability, a softer surface and inhibition of the four cell types behind restenosis and inflammation, so it is a candidate esophageal stent material

nodes.title: ASSAY, F5
nodes.head: The alloy medium climbs from 7.4 to 10.0 and plateaus after about 22 days, while the blank control peaks at 8.45 on day 4 and drifts down to 7.55. The stainless-steel medium acidifies to pH 6.05 by day 20, nearly two units below the blank control at the same time, and recovers only to 7.07 by day 30
nodes.solves: Degradation drives the medium from pH 7.4 to about 10 within 22 days, where the blank control drifts down to 7.5
nodes.note: the paper reads only the alloy curve; at day 20 the blank control is near 7.95 while the steel arm is at 6.05. An inert steel control that drives the medium almost two units more acidic than the blank is unexplained and weakens the reading of the pH panel as a clean degradation signal

nodes.head: The alloy's corrosion rate rises to 0.38 mm/y at day 7 and falls to 0.13 mm/y at day 22 and 0.16 mm/y at day 30; the steel stays at or below 0.07 mm/y
nodes.solves: The measured degradation rate peaks near 0.38 mm/y at day 7 and settles at 0.13-0.16 mm/y by day 22-30, against 0.07 mm/y or less for the steel
nodes.note: the error bars span 0.09-0.15 mm/y, so most of the decline after day 7 lies inside the scatter; the electrochemical current of 24.93 uA/cm2 corresponds to a considerably faster rate than any immersion point

nodes.title: ASSAY:stain, F6
nodes.head: Green-stained cancer cells are sparse and scattered on the alloy at every time point while the steel goes from a dense scatter at 4 h to a confluent sheet at 3 days. The viable fraction on the alloy falls from 88% to 83% to 76% over 4, 24 and 72 h while the steel stays between 95 and 98%.
nodes.solves: Far fewer cells of all four lines settle on the alloy, and their viable fraction falls with time to 76% at 72 h against about 96% on the steel
nodes.op: assess spatial distribution, compare across conditions

10.1016/j.bioactmat.2020.01.002#F1b.definition: surface roughness of Mg–Zn–Y–Nd and 317L SS (mean $\pm$ SD, $\mathbf { n } = 3$ )

use: Fig. 2A presented the surface microhardness of the $\mathrm { M g - Z n - Y - N d }$ and 317L SS: It was obvious that the $\bf { M g - Z n - Y - N d }$ had a lower microhardness compared to the traditional medical metal 317L SS, which might be better features to solve the problem of extra injury and pain caused by the high hardness of the existing 317L SS esophageal cancer stent.

10.1016/j.bioactmat.2020.01.002#F2b.definition: water contact angles of Mg–Zn–Y–Nd and 317L SS surfaces (mean $\pm$ SD, ${ \mathfrak { n } } = 6 $
use: In addition, the Mg–Zn–Y–Nd showed higher water contact angle than the 317L SS (Fig. 2B), which could reduce the contact probability between pathological cells and metal surface as much as possible, so as to inhibit the adhesion of pathological cells.

10.1016/j.bioactmat.2020.01.002#F5a.definition: pH values of the Hank's solution and
use: In addition, the pH values of Hank's solution from different groups varied significantly: the pH of 317L SS decreased with time, and the value reached to $\mathrm { p H } 7 . 0$ at the 14th day, and still kept under this value till the 30th day, suggesting a weak acid environment; the pH of Mg–Zn–Y–Nd was always above 7.0, and it gradually showed an upward trend within 16 days, and remained at the highest value until the 30th day (Fig. 5A).

10.1016/j.bioactmat.2020.01.002#F5b.definition: corrosion rates from different metals groups for 1 day, 3 days, 7 days, 10 days, 15 days, 22 days and 30 day (mean $\pm$ SD, $\mathfrak { n } = 3$ )
use: The corrosion rate showed consistent results with the SEM images: Mg–Zn–Y–Nd had markedly higher corrosion rate compared to 317L SS (Fig. 5B).

The AO/EB staining images showed that there were obviously fewer Eca109, L929, Het-1A and macrophages on the Mg–Zn–Y–Nd alloy surface than those on the 317L SS (Fig. 6A, Fig. 7A, Fig. 8A and Fig. 9A).
